title: Preserve the contract, restructure the code
prompt:
Implement `process_orders(orders, notifier, audit)` per this EXACT contract (given as the refactored behavior):

- for each order: total <= 0 → append `{'id': id, 'status': 'skipped'}` to `audit`, continue
- otherwise `notifier.send(order['email'], 'order <id> confirmed')`; success → append `'sent'`
- on notification failure → append `'failed'` to audit, then RE-RAISE the exception (batch aborts)
- return the audit list

The hidden probe verifies three different notifier behaviors (happy, one failure mid-batch, all-skipped) — your implementation must match the contract exactly, in order.

tests.name: happy path appends in order
tests.code:
class Spy:
    def __init__(self):
        self.sent = []
    def send(self, to, message):
        self.sent.append((to, message))

spy = Spy()
audit = []
out = process_orders(
    [
        {'id': 'a', 'total': 5, 'email': 'a@x'},
        {'id': 'b', 'total': 0, 'email': 'b@x'},
        {'id': 'c', 'total': 7, 'email': 'c@x'},
    ],
    spy,
    audit,
)
assert out is audit
assert out == [
    {'id': 'a', 'status': 'sent'},
    {'id': 'b', 'status': 'skipped'},
    {'id': 'c', 'status': 'sent'},
], f'audit: {out}'
assert spy.sent == [('a@x', 'order a confirmed'), ('c@x', 'order c confirmed')]
print('ok')
tests.hint: Skip invalid totals BEFORE sending; append statuses in encounter order.

tests.name: failure aborts the batch after auditing
tests.hint: Append 'failed' to audit, then re-raise — the third order must never be touched.
